requirements.title: a hello offering the v1 baseline is accepted and the response echoes v1
the negotiated capability list is the ordered intersection, v1 first, and never echoes an identifier the implementation does not implement
a hello without the v1 baseline is refused with the stable code unsupported, and an empty capability list is not an implicit wildcard
a frame whose version was never negotiated fails closed before its kind or body is interpreted
an unknown operation is answered with a res carrying the stable code unsupported, not a dropped request
no frame may precede the hello; a connection that opens with anything else is refused
every protocol failure carries one of the twelve stable error codes, so a caller can match on the code and never on the message
the handshake response names the lease interval and the control plane's grant-signing key, so a node can renew and verify offline
a peer that negotiated controller-epoch is told a nonzero epoch and persists it on every event, so a superseded controller's decisions are distinguishable
ws.create returns a workspace with an id, a generation and a state drawn from the lifecycle table
replaying a mutating request with the same idempotency key is a no-op that returns the original result
ws.ready gates claimed: a workspace reported claimed names the node holding it and a nonzero generation
ws.get of an id that does not exist is not_found, never an empty success
a mount path inside a system directory is refused with bad_request at create time
ws.list reports a created workspace at the same generation ws.get reports
destroyed is absorbing: after ws.destroy the workspace is gone or terminal and never returns to a serving state
a grant is issued only for a claimed workspace and binds client, workspace, node and generation
a grant request for a workspace that does not exist is refused, not answered with a grant for nothing
a node refuses a grant whose generation is not the workspace's current one
a node refuses a grant whose workspace does not match the request it accompanies
a node operation presented with no grant at all is refused
a move increments the generation, and every grant minted under the previous one stops working
an expired lease returns the workspace to pending with its last snapshot, and a node dying is the same event as a node moving
seq 0 of every session is the info chunk, so a replay from 0 reconstructs the session header
the exit chunk is the last chunk and the log is closed after it
chunk sequence numbers start at 0 and increase by exactly one, with no reordering and no hole
input is deduplicated by iseq: a retried keystroke at or below the last applied sequence is dropped, never typed twice
s.attach from 0 replays the retained log byte-identically through the same path as the live tail
s.wait reports the exit status the exit chunk carried, so a detached client learns the outcome
a replay from an evicted seq emits a gap chunk naming the lost range, continues from the oldest retained chunk, and does not kill the session
an attach past the produced range never fabricates output: the node reports where live begins and emits nothing before it
the bytes a process writes to stdout reach the client verbatim, on the stdout stream, with the exit status that ran them
the same tree always produces the same artifact id: a snapshot is deterministic, not merely reproducible in principle
an artifact id is the digest of its bytes and GET returns exactly those bytes
a workspace restored from a snapshot serves the files the source held
an ordinary snapshot is labelled live and is never reported authoritative, because it may have observed a changing tree
an unknown artifact is not found, and a digest held by another tenant is indistinguishable from one that does not exist
an upload is published only after its digest matches the id it was stored under
a move advances the generation and the destination serves the source tree: the filesystem, identity and policy travel
an authoritative snapshot quiesces the workspace, reports consistency quiesced, and only then becomes committable failover state
the workspace holds a placeholder and never the secret: the environment the node writes carries a reference, and the real value appears nowhere in the tree
a placeholder aimed at a host its binding does not cover blocks the request and records the decision as leak_blocked, rather than forwarding it
a destination no rule and no binding covers is denied before any byte is sent upstream
a destination resolving to a loopback, private, link-local or multicast address is refused unless explicitly allowed, which closes the metadata endpoint by default
no event payload carries the secret a binding holds; the audit record names the decision, not the credential
approval.get of an id that does not exist is not_found
approval.list returns pending rows unless a status is named, so a caller polling for work never sees a decided row as outstanding
an approve-mode request releases no upstream byte before a durable decision, and the row is idempotent on the request fingerprint
a second decision on a decided row is conflict, while a replay carrying the original idempotency key returns the row as decided
a decision is durable: it survives a control-plane restart and is still the answer the broker gets
agent.create returns a durable agent with a workspace, a derived status and an inbox, so nothing about the conversation lives only in a process
agent.message appends to the inbox and the message stays there until a turn consumes it
the inbox is bounded and refuses the excess with resource_exhausted rather than growing without limit
agent.transcript answers from the durable mirror with a page and a continuation cursor, and never wakes the workspace to do it
a transcript read below the oldest retained index names the evicted range as a gap, so a reader never sees a shorter log without being told
agent.sleep pauses the workspace and a later message wakes it, reporting that it did
agent.get of an id that does not exist is not_found
a destroyed agent is terminal and is never resurrected by a later message, wake or read
seq is assigned by the control plane and is the only total order: a tail is strictly increasing in seq
the canonical log is dense: a tail from the oldest retained sequence has no hole
a stream filter returns one workspace's whole history and nothing else
a state change that emits no event is a bug: creating and claiming a workspace emits ws.created, then ws.claiming, then ws.claimed, in that order
lifecycle events use the canonical type names, so a reader of another implementation's log recognises them
a tail from a sequence beyond the head returns nothing and no error, rather than blocking or inventing a page
an out-of-band append is assigned a sequence by the control plane and becomes visible in the canonical order
an out-of-band append carrying a field the implementation does not know is refused, rather than silently half-applied
an export cursor advances only after its destination accepts the bounded batch, so retries may duplicate but never skip
a request older than the retention watermark fails with evicted and names the oldest retained sequence; it never silently starts at a newer one
